column1: # The kept comment classes: every comment the strip leaves in place.
# This file is their one definition. The stripper and both verifiers read it.
# Columns, tab-separated: class, kind, languages, pattern, why.
#   directive    a tool reads the comment. Only the matching comment stays.
#   tool-block   a tool, or a rule that names the marker, reads the whole
#                block. Every comment in it stays.
#   prose        a reader must not break it. The whole block stays.
#   clap-derive  the pattern names derive macros. A doc comment on an item
#                that derives one is the item's --help text, and stays.
#   macro-doc    a doc comment inside a macro's input stays, since the macro
#                can read it. The pattern names the macros that only forward one.
#   unsupported  a form no proof covers. A file that holds one is refused.
#   typed-jsdoc  the pattern names a directive. In a file that holds it, every
#                `/**` comment stays: the compiler reads it as a type.
# languages: a comma list of rust, ts and css. `ts` covers JavaScript too.
# pattern: matched against one comment, from its first character. A directive
# or unsupported pattern sees each run of whitespace as one space. Keep it
# valid for both Python `re` and `grep -E`: no backslash-letter escapes.
# A clap-derive or macro-doc pattern must read `^(A|B)$`.
